glosses: marks the object of a stative predicate
(what is liked, understood, wanted, or perceived)
patterns.usage_note: With predicates that describe a state rather than an action — 好きだ, 嫌いだ, 上手だ, 苦手だ, 分かる, できる, 要る, 見える, 聞こえる, potentials, and 〜たい / 〜がほしい — the thing the state is about is marked with が, not を, while the experiencer takes は or が, and with 分かる, 見える, 聞こえる, 要る it may also take には. Learners who transfer English transitivity and write 日本語を分かる produce the classic mistake. を does turn up with 〜たい and with some potential verbs when the speaker stresses the action itself (水を飲みたい), but が is the default and the safe answer in short, simple clauses; を is normal once the object is separated from the predicate or the action itself is in focus.

examples.ruby: 帰[かえ]り道[みち]で、とにかく冷[つめ]たい水[みず]が飲[の]みたかった。
examples.english: On the walk home, all I wanted was a drink of cold water.

examples.ruby: 弟[おとうと]は昔[むかし]から蜘蛛[くも]が苦手[にがて]らしい。
examples.english: My little brother has apparently always been squeamish about spiders.

examples.ruby: 祖父[そふ]は今[いま]でも細[こま]かい字[じ]がよく見[み]えるらしい。
examples.english: My grandfather can still make out fine print perfectly well, it seems.
